MCP tool schemas arrive from the same local server after connection, so they are executable-interface context rather than duplicated host prompt text. The package drift gate additionally requires both hosts to carry the exact same Skill and
Every MCP tool is annotated read-only, non-destructive, idempotent, and closed-world.
The plugin declares no credentials, network service, lifecycle hooks, or pre-approved host tools.

The local stdio server reads only the repository path explicitly passed by the host. It returns structured findings and migration suggestions; it cannot edit files or execute suggested verification commands.
Repository files, including instruction-shaped files, are detector input. They cannot replace the packaged Skill, tool schemas, registry validation, or session verification state.
Codex and Claude manifests cannot contain detector, migration, or verification behavior. CI rejects missing, changed, or unexpected generated package files.

to obtain the exact published Offing version. Initial installation can access the npm registry and runs with the permissions of the host process; consumers that require an offline or pre-vetted supply chain should preinstall the package and configure the local executable instead.

Read-only MCP annotations describe Offing behavior but do not grant filesystem access. The host remains responsible for sandboxing, repository-path authorization, command approval, and review of any edits an agent makes after receiving migration context.

Repository parsing currently has no aggregate file-count, byte, depth, finding-count, or wall-time budget, and supported manifests and lockfiles are read in full. A malicious or accidentally huge repository can therefore exhaust CPU or memory in the local MCP process. The established impact is local availability only; no code execution, network access, or repository mutation path was found. Deployments scanning untrusted repositories should add external time/memory limits until Offing implements deterministic scanner budgets.

This deterministic gate evaluates the packaged host contracts and shared executable behavior; it does not claim that every future Codex or Claude model version will make identical autonomous routing choices. Live model observations and the
check may supplement this baseline, but they cannot replace or weaken the reproducible release gate. The eval also does not prove host sandbox configuration outside Offing's package.

A source-backed security review on 2026-10-15 found one low-severity local availability issue: the missing aggregate scanner budgets described above. It found no path for repository content to replace the workflow contract, inject built-in migration commands, execute suggested commands, open a network listener, or create host-specific executable behavior.
